column7: HAND ANALYSIS (not produced by tools/crystal_match.py). Crystal home/mobile.asm MobileAPI (00:3E32) vs Trainer 00:0150-018C (bytes verified by disassembly). Evidence: (1) ends with jp $4030 at 00:018A and 75:4030 is _MobileAPI (Crystal 44:4030; masked byte-match, only imm8 difference is the LOW() of a WRAM address); (2) same instruction sequence at the start: cp $02; ld [wMobileAPIIndex],a; ld a,l; ld [wc986],a; ld a,h; ld [wc987],a; jr nz - Trainer operands C825/C823/C824 are Crystal C988/C986/C987 shifted by -$163, consistent with analysis/crystal_ram_map.tsv; the fall-through part stores B/C at C820 (Crystal wc983) exactly like Crystal (ld hl,wc983; ld a,c; ld [hli],a; ld a,b; ld [hl],a); (3) sets bit 6 of C6C1 (Crystal: set 6,[wc822]; C822->C6C1 is a 33-function RAM-map entry (recount by the review; earlier text said 32)) before switching bank; (4) 52 Trainer call sites (banks 67/68) load an API index into A and call 00:0150 like Crystal callers (analysis/crystal_api_calls.tsv); (5) DIFFERS: bank switching is written for MBC5 (16-bit current bank in HRAM FF8A/FF8B, writes to $2000 and $3000) instead of Crystal rst Bankswitch (MBC3, one byte). Name imported from Crystal community disassembly.

HAND ANALYSIS. Crystal ReturnMobileAPI (00:3E60). Evidence: immediately follows MobileAPI in both ROMs (Crystal 3E32,3E60,3E80,3E93,3ED7 / Trainer 0150,018D,01B7,01ED,0247); stores A,L,H to the API-return variables, pops the saved bank, restores it, then RES 6 of C6C1 (= wc822 bit 6, set by MobileAPI) and reloads HL/A from the result variables; tool structural alignment 13/17 instructions (analysis/crystal_matches.tsv ReturnMobileAPI). Name imported from Crystal.

HAND ANALYSIS. Functional equivalent of Crystal Serial:: (the mobile branch) + home MobileReceive (00:3E80). Evidence: Trainer serial RAM vector CBFA = jp $01B7 (bytes at 00:04C8-04D6); 00:01B7 pushes AF/BC/DE/HL, saves the bank, switches to bank 75 and calls 75:56D2 (00:01D5), which is _MobileReceive (Crystal 44:56C5, masked match MEDIUM, imm8 diff = LOW() of C808->C6A8), restores the bank, pops and RETI. Differs from Crystal: no hMobileReceive test (Trainer has no link/printer alternatives on this vector) and the register push/reti is merged into this routine. Name imported from Crystal; Trainer role (serial interrupt handler) is CONFIRMED from the vector bytes, the identification with MobileReceive is PROBABLE.

HAND ANALYSIS. Crystal MobileTimer (00:3E93). Evidence: Trainer timer RAM vector CBF7 = jp $01ED (bytes 00:04B9-04C7); 00:01ED pushes AF/BC/DE/HL, xor a / ldh [rTAC],a, ldh a,[rIF] / and $1B / ldh [rIF],a, tests C709 (= wc86a) and bit 1 of C6C1 (= wc822) and rSC bit 7, switches to bank 75 and calls 75:58EA (00:0227) = _Timer (Crystal 44:58DE, masked byte-match HIGH), restores bank, reloads rTIMA from rTMA (ldh a,[$FF06]; ldh [$FF05],a) and re-arms rTAC=$06 (Crystal: 1<<rTAC_ON|rTAC_65536_HZ = $06), pops, RETI. Differs: no hMobile gate at entry. tool structural alignment 27/40. Name imported from Crystal.

HAND ANALYSIS. Crystal Function3ed7 (00:3ED7, marked "; unreferenced" in the Crystal source). Trainer 00:0247: saves A in D002 (Crystal: [$dc02]; DC02->D002 is the WRAMX shift in analysis/crystal_ram_map.tsv), saves the 16-bit bank (FF8A/FF8B), switches to bank 000F, calls 0F:4247 (= Crystal 45:4243 Function114243, guided match), restores the bank and reloads A from D002. Nobody calls 00:0247 in the Trainer ROM (no cd 47 02 in any bank). Adjacent to MobileTimer in both ROMs. Only the shape is shared; purpose unknown.
